/home/runner/work/understudy/understudy/understudy/agents/lens-content.md:44:Cross-check against the persona's own Q4 answer. **If your reading and theirs disagree, theirs wins** — they were there and you were not. Note the disagreement; it usually means the product is doing something subtler than either reading alone captures.
/home/runner/work/understudy/understudy/understudy/agents/lens-icp.md:34:Read, per persona: `session.log`, `persona-debrief.md`, `timeline.json`, `findings-raw.json`, and every screenshot cited. If the visit ran the **ICP sweep** (`visit-shapes.md`, Shape V-ICP) its screenshots are your primary evidence for pricing, proof and "for whom" language — open them all.
/home/runner/work/understudy/understudy/understudy/agents/lens-trust.md:53:- **⚑ Report only what the persona could verify from the site.** You may not check a company register, search for news, or use your own knowledge of the company. A trust finding sourced from outside the capture is not a finding about the site — and on a competitor's site in Mode D it is close to defamatory. **If the persona could not tell, the finding is "the site does not say", never "the company does not".**
/home/runner/work/understudy/understudy/understudy/agents/objectives-scorer.md:3:description: Scores the run objectives the user supplied at interview — achieved, partially achieved, not achieved, or not reachable — against the recorded evidence. Sees the expected outcome for the first time, after capture is complete. Runs only when the run has objectives. Use after capture, alongside the scoring lenses.
/home/runner/work/understudy/understudy/understudy/commands/report.md:17:Capture is the expensive, irreversible part; scoring is cheap and repeatable. Separating them means:
/home/runner/work/understudy/understudy/understudy/commands/report.md:71:**If the run has objectives**, also dispatch `objectives-scorer` — it reads the expected outcomes for the first time, after capture is fixed.
/home/runner/work/understudy/understudy/understudy/commands/run.md:131:| **A — Journey** | `traversal-journey` — one traversal per persona | ux · bugs · onboarding · content · icp | yes |
/home/runner/work/understudy/understudy/understudy/commands/run.md:132:| **A-visit — Visit** | `traversal-visit` — one visit per persona | clarity · conversion · trust · icp | yes |
/home/runner/work/understudy/understudy/understudy/commands/run.md:205:**One capture, N scorings, in parallel.** The Mode-A lenses all read the same traversal — this is the whole point of the architecture, and running one agent per objective through the product would cost ~4× for identical evidence.
/home/runner/work/understudy/understudy/understudy/commands/run.md:222:**If the run has objectives**, also dispatch `objectives-scorer` — it reads the expected outcomes for the first time, after capture is fixed.
/home/runner/work/understudy/understudy/understudy/evals/README.md:20:Capture is the expensive, irreversible half; scoring is cheap and needs no
/home/runner/work/understudy/understudy/understudy/evals/behaviour/mode-arithmetic-website/graders/criteria.md:1:- The answer says TWO captures for one persona: one persona visit (Mode A-visit) that clarity, conversion and trust all score, and one crawl (Mode C) for seo. Stating it as a formula — one visit per persona plus one crawl, so two here — also passes, as long as the two-capture case is stated.
/home/runner/work/understudy/understudy/understudy/evals/behaviour/mode-arithmetic-website/graders/criteria.md:2:- It does not propose one capture per lens.
/home/runner/work/understudy/understudy/understudy/evals/results/2026-09-11T0957Z/product-onboarding-run1/findings-final.md:175:- Whether the novice's guessed workspace type changed anything she saw — only one type was exercised per persona.
/home/runner/work/understudy/understudy/understudy/evals/results/2026-09-14T1120Z/site-trust-run1/findings-final.md:203:- One device per persona; a trust severity flip between a sceptic and an eager buyer could not be observed on pricing, because the sceptic never looked for it.
/home/runner/work/understudy/understudy/understudy/evals/results/2026-09-14T1144Z/product-onboarding-run1/findings-final.md:151:- Only one of the three workspace types was exercised per persona; "Sovereign vault" was never selected.
/home/runner/work/understudy/understudy/understudy/evals/results/2026-10-05T1320Z/product-bugs-run1/findings-final.md:87:- Settings "Federated graph replication" default-on may not match the signup choice (power-user chose Federated graph, novice chose Hybrid mesh) — settings state was not compared per persona.
/home/runner/work/understudy/understudy/understudy/evals/results/2026-10-19T1141Z/site-conversion-run1/findings-final.md:10:- Size of every recommended change is untested: this run had one visitor per persona and no traffic data
/home/runner/work/understudy/understudy/understudy/evals/results/baseline-x3-product/product-onboarding-run1/findings-final.md:4:- Framework: Layer C activation (C-TTFV, C-STEPS, C-ABANDON, C-SOWHAT) + first-value definition; funnel built from `timeline.json` per persona
/home/runner/work/understudy/understudy/understudy/evals/results/baseline-x3-product/product-onboarding-run1/findings-final.md:199:- Single session per persona; the "returned to a second task" stage could only be inferred from in-session retries.
/home/runner/work/understudy/understudy/understudy/evals/results/baseline-x3-site/site-trust-run2/findings-final.md:198:- Single visit per persona; the objective "find price without giving an email" was attempted by one persona only.
/home/runner/work/understudy/understudy/understudy/references/first-value.md:84:**Promise-match failures are persona-specific by definition.** The same onboarding passes for one persona and fails for another, because they arrived with different promises. Pass 2 reports the score per persona and **flags any finding whose severity flips across personas** — a flip is usually the most interesting thing in the report, and averaging it away is how it gets lost.

/home/runner/work/understudy/understudy/understudy/references/playwright-patterns.md:28:| `browser_close()` | Close the tab. **Does not clear state** — see *Fresh context per persona* |
/home/runner/work/understudy/understudy/understudy/references/playwright-patterns.md:117:**Fresh context per persona — reset, then verify. `browser_close()` is not a reset.**
/home/runner/work/understudy/understudy/understudy/references/severity-rubric.md:29:- **Severity is per persona.** If the same behaviour is P1 for one persona and a non-issue for another, that is two findings, not an average. See `report-template.md`.
/home/runner/work/understudy/understudy/understudy/references/visit-shapes.md:26:2. Fresh browser context per persona. **Logged out.** Clear any prior state — a site that recognises you is not the site a visitor meets.
/home/runner/work/understudy/understudy/understudy/references/visit-shapes.md:195:## Artifacts, per persona
/home/runner/work/understudy/understudy/understudy/skills/onboarding/SKILL.md:52:      ~90 min per persona.
/home/runner/work/understudy/understudy/understudy/skills/onboarding/SKILL.md:56:      ~15–25 min per persona, plus a crawl.
/home/runner/work/understudy/understudy/understudy/skills/onboarding/SKILL.md:227:## Step 4 — Device profile per persona
/home/runner/work/understudy/understudy/understudy/skills/onboarding/SKILL.md:229:Ask per persona, not once for all. A persona who is mobile-dominant and one who is desktop-only are testing different products.
/home/runner/work/understudy/understudy/understudy/skills/onboarding/SKILL.md:299:Default: **90 minutes** per persona, with a hard stop.
/home/runner/work/understudy/understudy/understudy/skills/onboarding/SKILL.md:341:> Which email should the persona sign up with? I'll extend it per persona and per run — `you+novice-20260911@yourdomain` — so every run is a fresh signup. It goes in the target file as `alias_email`.
/home/runner/work/understudy/understudy/understudy/skills/traversal-compare/SKILL.md:25:You cannot human-in-the-loop past a competitor's auth wall, and you must not try. **Never create an account on a site the user does not own.** Never submit a form, request a demo, start a trial, or contact anyone. A competitor capture is read-only, and this is not negotiable — it is someone else's business, and a lead in their CRM is a real cost you have imposed on them.
/home/runner/work/understudy/understudy/understudy/skills/traversal-compare/SKILL.md:76:1. Reset the browser first (`playwright-patterns.md`, *Fresh context per persona*) — `browser_close()` alone carries the previous site's cookies and dismissed popups into this one. Fresh context, logged out, no shared state. Its result goes into `site.json` as `setup_state`.
/home/runner/work/understudy/understudy/understudy/skills/traversal-journey/SKILL.md:50:Fresh browser context — run the reset from `playwright-patterns.md` (*Fresh context per persona*) **before** any auth wall, and write its result into `timeline.json` as `setup_state`. `browser_close()` alone leaves the previous persona's cookies behind. Set the viewport per `playwright-patterns.md` — **and verify it.** An unverified viewport means a device-defined persona may be testing the wrong product, invisibly.
/home/runner/work/understudy/understudy/understudy/skills/traversal-measure/SKILL.md:40:1. **Fresh browser context.** A warm cache measures your second visit, not a visitor's first. Run the reset from `playwright-patterns.md` (*Fresh context per persona*) before each page and viewport — it clears the HTTP cache too — and put its result in the record as `setup_state`.

That's **2 captures**:

1. **Mode A-visit, one persona visit.** Clarity, conversion and trust all score this same capture. You get one capture and three scorings, not three captures (`commands/run.md:205`).
2. **Mode C, one crawl.** SEO is scored from this. A crawl uses no persona, so the number of personas doesn't change it.

The general rule is one visit per persona plus one crawl. With one persona, that's 1 + 1 = 2.
